steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Language analysis examines how writers choose and use words, phrases and literary devices to create specific effects on the reader.

steps.title: Alliteration
steps.body: Repetition of consonant sounds for emphasis or musicality. "The slippery snake slithered silently."

steps.title: Onomatopoeia
steps.body: Words that sound like what they describe. "Crash, bang, hiss, whisper."

steps.title: Sibilance
steps.body: Repeated 's' sounds creating a hissing effect. "The soft, silky snake slid through the grass."

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the difference between a metaphor and a simile? | What does PEEL stand for? | Why should you avoid writing "this makes the reader want to read on"?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A metaphor directly says something IS something else, while a simile compares using "like" or "as". | Point, Evidence, Explain, Link - a structure for writing analytical paragraphs. | It's too vague and generic - you need to explain the specific emotional or intellectual response created.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use precise terminology but focus on effects Embed short quotations into your sentences Consider the writer's purpose and context Focus on depth over breadth - analyse fewer features in more detail Use phrases like "this suggests", "this conveys", "this implies" Always link back to the question focus
